The features make managing money incredibly easy: • Get paid up to a day early when your salary is due. • Savings Pots help you organise money for different goals. • Savings Challenges make saving more engaging and motivating. • Cashback offers help you earn money back on everyday spending. • Monzo Perks and Extra provide valuable benefits and additional features. • Instant spending notifications keep you in complete control of your finances. • Budgeting tools make it easy to track where every penny goes. The app is simple, modern, and reliable, and the customer service has always been responsive whenever I’ve needed help. My recent experience proved to me that Monzo is a bank that values its customers and is willing to put things right when mistakes happen. In response to a repeat of what I already know from you. Dear Starling Bank Limited, Re: Public response to my app store review, failure to make reasonable adjustments under the Equality Act 2010 (ongoing complaint, disability: dyslexia/neurodivergence) I am writing formally in response to the reply your team posted to my app store review regarding the change from a 4-digit to a 6-digit passcode. I do not accept the substance of that response, and I am putting the following on record. 1. This is not a resolution — it is a restatement of the barrier Your response confirms that Starling intends to proceed with the 6-digit passcode requirement, citing security as the justification. At no point does your response engage with the reasonable adjustment I have specifically requested: retention of a 4-digit passcode, or an equivalent alternative that does not increase the cognitive load involved in recalling and entering a sequence of digits under time pressure. Citing “security” as a blanket justification, without any individual assessment of my circumstances, does not discharge your duty under section 20 of the Equality Act 2010. The duty to make reasonable adjustments is anticipatory and individual; a policy applied uniformly to all customers is not, by itself, a reasonable adjustment, and can itself be the source of indirect discrimination under section 19. 2. Face ID/fingerprint is not a substitute for a reasonable adjustment Your response suggests Face ID or fingerprint login as an alternative “if your device supports it.” This is conditional, not universal, and does not address the situations in which the passcode itself must still be entered, including app updates, new device setup, and, critically, payee authentication. Your response does not mention, and has consistently failed to mention, that customers are required to re-enter the passcode when adding or paying a new payee, and that this is done under a countdown timer before the session times out. This omission is not incidental. It is the single most disabling part of this process for me: being required to accurately recall and input a longer numeric sequence, under time pressure, in order to complete an everyday banking task. That is a barrier to my use of your service, and it is one your public response has again failed to acknowledge, let alone address. 3. This is not a new issue I have been raising the impact of dyslexia and neurodivergence on my ability to use Starling’s app with you for approximately two years. A previous complaint on this subject was upheld, and compensation was paid to me in recognition of the difficulties I experienced. Despite that finding, no adjustment has been implemented in the intervening period, and the current change moves further away from accessibility, not towards it. A business that has already acknowledged, through an upheld complaint and payment of compensation, that its systems disadvantage me on the grounds of disability, and then proceeds to introduce a change that increases that disadvantage without individual assessment, cannot reasonably claim it was unaware of the impact. On the information available to me, this reads as a continuation of the same failure, not an isolated decision. 4. What I require 1. Written confirmation of whether Starling will individually assess my request to retain a 4-digit passcode, or provide an equivalent adjustment, as a reasonable adjustment under section 20 of the Equality Act 2010. 2. An explanation, in writing, of how payee authentication and session timeout will operate for disabled customers who cannot reliably enter a 6-digit code within the current time limit, and what adjustment is available for that specific step. 3. Confirmation of what steps, if any, have been taken since my previous upheld complaint to implement the adjustments that complaint identified as necessary. I am giving you 14 days from the date of this letter to respond substantively to the three points above. If I do not receive a response that engages with these points — rather than a repetition of the general security justification already given — I will refer this matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service, and I reserve the right to pursue this further, including under the Equality Act 2010, in respect of both the original complaint and this further failure to adjust.
